messages:
eval-bot: nightly-eval alert: pset_v48 -> v49 caused 6.2% drop on intent_f1 across customer-facing promptset A. failing cases concentrated on negative/neutral labels, see report: https://internal.redd/evals/1718809999

maria: on it. quick diff of the pset committed yesterday?

zach: PR #4523 merged the prompt examples rename + labelmap consolidation, commit d3f4b2. suspect label_map reordering.

ojas: failing examples look like label flip from `none` -> `negated` in several canonical examples. quick grep showed label_map = ["pos","none","neg"] in v48 but v49 has ["pos","neg","none"].

lee: that ordering change would shift the integer indices used in eval harness, yep. eval harness expects stable index assignments unless we rebaseline.

maria: dump of the failing summary (top 3):
```
pset A: 1200 examples
regressions: 74 failing by label mismatch
sample: id: 9921 expected: none got: negated
id: 9933 expected: none got: negated
id: 9978 expected: pos got: pos (ok)
```

zach: my bad, the consolidation PR included an automated labelset-sort step to make tests deterministic, but we didn't update the mapping used by the nightly eval job. PR linked: https://git.redd/p/4523

ojas: two options: 1) revert mapping change to preserve previous indices, 2) rebaseline nightly expected labels and run small canary. prefer 2 if product ok.

product-signer: product here — rebaseline can be OK if we confirm no semantic label meaning changed. From notes, seems purely ordering. need sign-off and a short changelog for customers.

lee: agree with canary. propose: create a rebaseline PR that includes mapping file + unit update + a 24h canary on nightly. also add a fast validator that compares sample label texts before committing.

maria: I'll draft the rebaseline PR and include a checklist: "verify label text equality, run eval harness locally, run 2-nightly windows canary". pinging @product-signer for approval thread.

product-signer: approved for canary. please add a customer-facing note in the changelog and a rollback plan.

zach: opened 1718810201-rebaseline-psetA-labelmap branch with changes and smoke tests. link: https://git.redd/p/rebase-1718810201

eval-bot: scheduled a canary run for 1718810600 against 10% traffic and 500 random examples from pset A. will report back in thread. :robot_face:

maria: thanks all — let's keep this tight. if canary passes we'll merge and publish rebaseline; if not, revert PR #4523. :thumbsup:

lee: also adding a small lint to the pset CI to fail on labelset reorders without explicit bump file.

zach: again, sorry for the churn — learned to pin label indices in the harness.

omnis: (automated) canary started: run_id=canary-1718810600

eval-bot: canary complete: no significant regressions on the 500-sample canary. detailed diff: https://internal.redd/evals/canary-1718810600/diff

product-signer: ok to ship rebaseline. maria please coordinate release note.

maria: will do, pushing PR to prod and drafting changelog paragraph now.

zach: bumping the retrospective item: "ensure labelset changes include explicit rebaseline ticket".

lee: filed infra task #789 to add label-order linter to pset CI.

maria: closing loop here — thanks team.
